Going Linux · Hardware Designed for Linux

Hardware is not designed for Linux. But serious hardware vendors have their drivers in the kernel when their product launches.

Sadly preinstalled Linux usually sucks badly, probably worse than Mac and Win. Since hardware vendors treat it like Android instead of joining with a distro.

I haven't had significant hardware compatability issues for years.

I've got an issue on one of my laptops where the wifi driver reports the wrong connection speed to iwconfig. Apart from that, it's all good. No faffing around recompiling kernels and tweaking for days.

I do not want to say anything to prevent people from supporting System 76 or any other vendor selling equipment with Linux pre-installed. Please, support them.

That said, I've installed various flavors of Linux on nearly a dozen laptops and at least the desktops in the past 12-15 months. The only thing I have found to not work has been NetGear and Belkin USB wifi dongles for desktops. Everything else just works. The hardware manufacturers largely ignore Linux, but the kernel maintainers clearly are ahead of the curve now.
